u0: This is the normal working state: no box-recovery obligation is pending and the exit-carry rule has not been violated. The box may be held or lying on the floor, and the agent can move through the room, pick it up, put it down, or head for the exit. If the box falls, a one-step recovery obligation begins; if the agent reaches the exit without carrying the box, the state becomes a penalized exit-without-box condition. Reaching the exit while holding the box satisfies the exit requirement when the episode ends.
u1: A box fall has just occurred and the agent is empty-handed, so a strict one-step recovery obligation is pending. On the very next step the agent must end up holding the box again; if it does, the obligation clears and normal progress resumes. Remaining empty-handed, suffering another fall without holding, or reaching the exit without the box breaks the recovery rule and causes irreversible failure.
u2: The agent has reached the exit without the box in hand, so the exit-carry requirement is unmet and a penalty is incurred; no fresh fall-recovery obligation is pending. In an ordinary episode this exit ends play without the exit payoff. If play could continue, holding the box on a later step without a new fall would clear the unmet exit condition, while a fall before that would create a compounded problem.
u3: Both the unmet exit-carry condition and a fresh fall are pending: the exit has been reached without the box, and the agent is empty-handed after the box fell. The agent must be holding the box on the next step without a new fall to clear both problems and return to normal progress. Staying empty-handed, or another fall while empty-handed, makes the failure irreversible.
u4: A mandatory recovery requirement has been broken for good: after a box fall, the agent did not end up holding the box on the immediately following step, or an additional fall occurred before recovery. Successful completion is no longer possible, and no later action can restore progress.
